newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann launches low D2 billing plan.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann launches low D2 billing plan.

text.p: Mannesmann Mobilfunk GmbH, the mobile communications group, said on Thursday it would introduce a low introductory rate for new customers and closed the first so-called roaming deal in the United States.

For a period of six months, new users will receive mobile phone services from its D2 digital cellular network for 29.95 marks ($17.66) a month. Afterward, new users can switch to other billing models at no charge.
The new billing plan takes effect on April 1.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk Chairman Juergen von Kuczkowski told a news conference at the CeBIT information technology trade fair that the service now had some 2.5 million subscribers and increasing volume of subscribers to cellular data services.
The D2 network is based on the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) standard. While GSM has been widely accepted internationally, it is only now beginning to find use in the United States.

In the past, GSM subscribers who went to the U.S. needed to use a separate phone compatible with the local mobile phone standard. In other countries it was possible through so-called roaming agreements for D2 subscribers to use other GSM networks to make calls with their own phone and be reachable at their number.
